title: What Arctic Dome Cities Is
definition: Arctic Dome Cities: warm cities under domes in the far north.
description:
Strip Arctic Dome Cities to its essence and you get warm cities under domes in the far north. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Cities & Habitats: first heated districts understanding, then snow transit prototypes, then insulation shells operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of dome hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Arctic Dome Cities
title: Real Research Today: Arctic Dome Cities
definition: Today's documented research behind Arctic Dome Cities.
description:
The road to Arctic Dome Cities is already being paved. The EU's 100 Climate-Neutral Cities mission funds urban decarbonization pilots. China's sponge city program rebuilds urban water systems to absorb floodwater.

Arcology concepts trace to architect Paolo Soleri's 1960s designs for hyper-dense eco-cities. Together these programs form the heated districts foundation that Arctic Dome Cities will build on — the snow transit results, the insulation shells methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as snow transit research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — The first dome hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first dome hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Arctic Dome Cities roadmap.
description:
The first dome hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its heated districts grid and snow transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the heated districts results have to replicate outside the lab, snow transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and insulation shells operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed heated districts demonstrations, snow transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting insulation shells uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Arctic Dome Cities
definition: Estimates Arctic Dome Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Arctic Dome Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a dome hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Arctic Dome Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Arctic Dome Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 84927 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where heated districts monitoring, snow transit redundancy, or insulation shells maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Arctic Dome Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Arctic Dome Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Arctic Dome Cities — warm cities under domes in the far north.

Phase 1 — Prove (heated districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (snow transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (insulation shells): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (thermal blocks): dome hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and arctic-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
